qualifying_findings.title: AWS API MCP Server policy normalization bypass
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary vendor security bulletin with CVE and coordinated-disclosure acknowledgement
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: AWS disclosed that custom-policy operation-name normalization in AWS API MCP Server could let operations containing consecutive capital letters fail to match a configured denyList or elicitList, potentially bypassing a denial or elicitation requirement.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: >= 0.2.13 and < 1.5.1; policy enforcement between an AI assistant's requested AWS API operation and the operator's configured guardrail.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server to 1.5.1 or later; AWS states there is no workaround other than upgrading and asks forks or derivatives to incorporate the fix.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP server that lets an assistant manage AWS accounts must enforce least-privilege and approval policy at the tool boundary; this defect could turn a nominally denied or approval-gated API operation into an executable action.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AWS and the AWS API MCP Server's general product coverage belong in ai-wiki. Retain the policy-bypass disclosure, affected authorization boundary, and upgrade requirement in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Microsoft Aspire CLI MCP configuration scanner leaks temporary diagnostics
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary Microsoft security advisory published in the Microsoft Aspire repository and reviewed by GitHub Advisory Database
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Microsoft states that insecure temporary files used by the deprecated Aspire CLI MCP configuration scanner can expose sensitive configuration information to a local attacker on a shared non-Windows temporary directory.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Aspire CLI 13.2.0 through 13.6.4; npm packages >= 13.4.2 and < 13.6.5; Linux and macOS. The affected component is the deprecated MCP configuration scanner used by agent or MCP initialization commands.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade Aspire CLI and its platform-specific package dependencies to 13.6.5 or later; a .NET SDK/runtime update alone does not establish that the CLI is patched.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local agent/MCP setup can expose configuration containing endpoints or credentials. Shared-temp handling is therefore a data-security and least-privilege boundary, even when the affected scanner is deprecated.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Microsoft and Aspire product context belong in ai-wiki; development-tool workflow context belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Keep this local-platform information-disclosure boundary and patch evidence in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP filesystem server same-device move race
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A source-parent symlink swap after validation can make server-filesystem move an outside file into an allowed directory, where subsequent read tools can expose it.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem < 2.3.0; patched 2.3.0. The reported boundary is the allowed-directory confinement model during same-device move_file.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Filesystem MCP tools are authority-bearing agents; a TOCTOU escape invalidates the directory boundary on which tool permissions depend.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog context belongs in ai-wiki; retain this confinement disclosure and patch boundary locally.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP fetch server IPv6 SSRF classifier gap
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: mcp-server-fetch classified IPv6 site-local fec0::/10 as public, allowing a request to pass its non-public-destination SSRF guard; the advisory notes limited default-host reachability and does not claim a demonstrated metadata-service read.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-server-fetch >= 2026.10.10 and < 2026.11.11; patched 2026.11.11. Boundary: fetch-tool network destination validation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An agent's fetch tool must constrain network authority outside the model; classification gaps can route tool calls to non-public addresses.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog context belongs in ai-wiki; retain this SSRF guard and upgrade evidence locally.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP Git server runs repository-controlled Git configuration
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: mcp-server-git could execute a program selected by an untrusted repository's Git configuration, including from a nominally read-only tool. The advisory says 2026.11.11 neutralizes command-bearing Git configuration and refuses Git older than 2.31.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-server-git < 2026.11.11; patched 2026.11.11. Boundary: repository configuration accepted by a Git-backed MCP server.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A tool marked read-only can still cross into code execution if repository metadata is treated as trusted, making this a delegated-authority and supply-chain risk.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog and general coding workflow belong upstream; retain this untrusted-repository execution path and patch evidence locally.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP fetch server robots path-canonicalization bypass
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: mcp-server-fetch could bypass a robots.txt disallow rule through path canonicalization differences such as //private versus /private.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-server-fetch >= 0.6.1 and < 2026.11.11; patched 2026.11.11. Boundary: content-access policy enforced by fetch path handling.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool-level content restrictions are part of agent data-access governance; path normalization needs to align with the policy interpreter.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog context belongs in ai-wiki; retain this policy-enforcement bypass locally.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP Git server repository-confinement bypass after prior fix
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The advisory reports that objects/info/alternates and linked-worktree common_dir handling could bypass the mcp-server-git --repository confinement after the earlier validation fix.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-server-git >= 2026.10.28 and < 2026.11.11; patched 2026.11.11. Boundary: --repository filesystem confinement.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository scoping is a least-privilege control for coding agents; incomplete fixes must be validated against Git's alternate object and worktree semantics.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog and general coding workflow belong upstream; retain the local security-control regression and patch evidence.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP filesystem server read race escapes allowed directories
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: A symlink swap after validation can cause read_text_file to return a file outside server-filesystem's allowedDirectories.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local files are often high-value agent context; a race that bypasses an allowed-directory control can disclose data beyond the delegated tool scope.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP server catalog context belongs in ai-wiki; retain this file-access security boundary and patch evidence locally.
